English

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Italian, Catalan, Portuguese, and Maltese festa. Doublet of fete, fiesta, feast, and fest.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈfɛstə/
  • Rhymes: -ɛstə

Noun

[edit]

festa (plural festas)

  1. A public holiday or feast day in Italy, Portugal, etc.

Anagrams

[edit]
  • fetas, TAFEs, Feast, feats, Fates, feast, fates, atefs

Basque

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Spanish fiesta.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /fes̺ta/ [fes̺.t̪a]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -es̺ta, -a
  • Hyphenation: fes‧ta

Noun

[edit]

festa inan

  1. feast, festival
    Synonyms: besta, jai
  2. party, partying
    Synonym: parranda

Catalan

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Late Latin fēsta, from the plural of Latin fēstum. Compare Occitan fèsta or hèsta.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central, Balearic) [ˈfes.tə]
  • IPA(key): (Valencia) [ˈfes.ta]
  • Audio (Barcelona):(file)
  • Rhymes: -esta

Noun

[edit]

festa f (plural festes)

  1. celebration; party

Derived terms

[edit]
  • festaire
  • festejar
  • fester
  • festívol
  • festós

Related terms

[edit]
  • festí
  • festiu
  • festival
  • festivar
  • festivitat

Further reading

[edit]
  • “festa”, in Diccionari de la llengua catalana [Dictionary of the Catalan Language] (in Catalan), second edition, Institute of Catalan Studies [Catalan: Institut d'Estudis Catalans], April 2007
  • “festa”, in Gran Diccionari de la Llengua Catalana, Grup Enciclopèdia Catalana, 2026
  • “festa” in Diccionari normatiu valencià, Acadèmia Valenciana de la Llengua.
  • “festa” in Diccionari català-valencià-balear, Antoni Maria Alcover and Francesc de Borja Moll, 1962.

Adjective

Fala

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese festa, from Late Latin fēsta.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈfesta/
  • Rhymes: -esta
  • Syllabification: fes‧ta

Noun

[edit]

festa f (plural festas)

  1. party
  2. festivity, holiday
    Synonyms: festividai, fistiviai, fistividai

Related terms

[edit]
  • festival (“festival”)
  • festividai (“festivity”)
  • festivu (“festive”)
  • fistival (“festival”)
  • fistiviai (“festivity”)
  • fistividai (“festivity”)
  • fistivu (“festive”)

References

[edit]

Galician

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Old Galician-Portuguese festa, from Late Latin fēsta, from the plural of Latin fēstum.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈfɛs̺tɐ]

Noun

[edit]

festa f (plural festas)

  1. festival
    Synonyms: feira, festival
  2. party
    Synonym: esmorga
  3. holiday; festivity
    Synonyms: día de festa, día festivo, día santo

Italian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

    From Late Latin fēsta, from the plural of Latin fēstus (“festive”).

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): /ˈfɛs.ta/
    • Audio (IT):(file)
    • Rhymes: -ɛsta
    • Hyphenation: fè‧sta

    Noun

    [edit]

    festa f (plural feste)

    1. feast
    2. holiday (civil)
    3. (in the plural) holidays (British), vacation (US)
    4. fair (often in combination)

    Descendants

    [edit]
    • → Japanese: フェスタ
    • → Maltese: festa (or from Sicilian)

    Anagrams

    [edit]
    • sfate

    Latin

    [edit]

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • fēsta:
      • (Classical Latin) IPA(key): [ˈfeːs.ta]
      • (modern Italianate Ecclesiastical) IPA(key): [ˈfɛs.ta]
    • fēstā:
      • (Classical Latin) IPA(key): [ˈfeːs.taː]
      • (modern Italianate Ecclesiastical) IPA(key): [ˈfɛs.ta]

    Etymology 1

    [edit]

    From the plural of fēstum. See main entry there for more.

    Noun

    [edit]

    fēsta f (genitive fēstae); first declension

    1. (Medieval Latin) party, feast

    [edit]

    singular plural

    dative fēstae fēstīs
    accusative fēstam fēstās
    ablative fēstā fēstīs
    vocative fēsta fēstae
    Descendants

    See descendants under fēstum.

    [edit]

    Noun

    [edit]

    fēsta

    1. nominative/accusative/vocative neuter plural of fēstum

    Adjective

    [edit]

    fēsta

      1. nominative/vocative feminine singular
      2. nominative/accusative/vocative neuter plural

    Adjective

    [edit]

    1. ablative feminine singular of fēstus

    Ligurian

    [edit]

    Macanese

    [edit]

    Etymology

    [edit]

    From Portuguese festa.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): /ˈfɛʃtɐ/, /ˈfɛstɐ/

    Noun

    [edit]

    festa

    1. party, fete, gala
      Synonym: fonçám
      festa di quebrâ testa ― big party; solemn commemoration (literally, “party of break forehead”)
      festa di fichâ ano ― birthday party
    2. celebration
    3. festival
      Quelê-tánto náchi-náchi na festa
      There were many Chinese people at the festival
    4. (religion) feast
      missa festa ― high mass (literally, “mass feast”)

    Related terms

    [edit]
    • bô-festa

    References

    [edit]
    • https://www.macaneselibrary.org/pub/english/uipatua.htm

    Maltese

    [edit]

    Etymology

    [edit]

    Borrowed from Sicilian festa and/or Italian festa.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): /ˈfɛːs.ta/
    • Rhymes: -ɛːsta

    Noun

    [edit]

    festa f (plural festi, diminutive festin)

    1. festivity, feast
      Synonyms: festività, għors (obsolete)
    2. feast, celebration, party
    3. name day
    4. holiday, vacation

    Related terms

    [edit]
    • festiv
    • festività
    • ffesteġġja
    • fottifesti (“killjoy”)

    Norwegian Nynorsk

    [edit]

    Etymology 1

    [edit]

    From Old Norse festa, from Proto-Germanic *fastijaną. Factitive of fast (“(stead)fast”).

    (rent farming land): Calque of Danish fæste.

    Alternative forms

    [edit]
    • feste (e- and split infinitives)

    Verb

    [edit]

    festa (present tense festar or fester, past tense festa or feste, past participle festa or fest, present participle festande, imperative fest)

    1. to fasten, to make fast
    2. to rent a farming land, to copyhold
      Synonym: bygsla
    Related terms
    [edit]
    • fast
    • fest f
    • feste n

    Etymology 2

    [edit]

    From fest +‎ -a, the first part being derived from Latin festum.

    Alternative forms

    [edit]
    • feste (e- and split infinitives)

    Verb

    [edit]

    festa (present tense festar, past tense festa, past participle festa, passive infinitive festast, present participle festande, imperative festa/fest)

    1. to party

    Etymology 3

    [edit]

    See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

    Alternative forms

    [edit]
    • festi (non-standard since 2012)

    Noun

    [edit]

    festa

    1. definite singular of fest f
    2. definite plural of feste n

    References

    [edit]
    • “festa” in The Nynorsk Dictionary.

    Anagrams

    [edit]
    • faste

    Old Irish

    [edit]

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): /ˈɸʲes.t̪a/

    Etymology 1

    [edit]

    From earlier fecht (“occasion”) +‎ -sa (“this”).

    Adverb

    [edit]

    festa

    1. now, forthwith
    2. henceforth
    Derived terms
    [edit]
    • feasta

    Etymology 2

    [edit]

    Verb

    [edit]

    ·festa

    1. second-person singular past subjunctive/conditional prototonic of ro·finnadar

    Mutation

    [edit]
    Mutation of ·festa
    radical lenition nasalization
    ·festa ·ḟesta ·festa
    pronounced with /β̃ʲ-/

    Note: Certain mutated forms of some words can never occur in Old Irish.
    All possible mutated forms are displayed for convenience.

    Portuguese

    [edit]

    Etymology 1

    [edit]
    Portuguese Wikipedia has an article on:
    festa
    Wikipedia pt

    From Old Galician-Portuguese festa, from Late Latin fēsta, from the plural of Latin fēstum.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
     
    • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈfɛs.tɐ/
    • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈfɛs.tɐ/
      • (Rio de Janeiro) IPA(key): /ˈfɛʃ.tɐ/
      • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈfɛs.ta/
    • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈfɛʃ.tɐ/

    • Rhymes: (Brazil) -ɛstɐ, (Portugal, Rio de Janeiro) -ɛʃtɐ
    • Hyphenation: fes‧ta

    Noun

    [edit]

    festa f (plural festas, diminutive festinha or festazinha or festim, augmentative festona or festão)

    1. party
      Vamos começar a festa. ― Let's get the party started.
      A festa acabou. ― The party's over.
    2. celebration
    3. festival
    4. (religion) feast
    5. (figurative) caress
      Synonyms: festinha, afago, carinho, carícia, mimo
      Fazer festas ao gato. ― Pet the cat.
